claims.text: High-energy mechanical alloying followed by rapid spark plasma sintering suppresses porosity in CoCrFeNiTi.
The proposed process produces a nanocrystalline solid solution dominated by FCC with a minor BCC phase.
Mechanical alloying and rapid SPS suppress formation of brittle HCP phase.
The proposed mechanical-alloying treatment is 40 h at 250 RPM.
The proposed SPS temperature range for dual-phase stability is 900–1100 °C.
A heating rate above 100 °C/min promotes the targeted phase state and limits decomposition.
The proposed SPS dwell time is 5 min.
Keeping the strain rate below 10^-3 s^-1 during sintering minimizes cracking caused by thermal-expansion mismatch.
Severe plastic deformation during mechanical alloying homogenizes the alloy.
Severe plastic deformation during mechanical alloying suppresses HCP nucleation.
Rapid SPS achieves full density while retaining grain refinement.
Rapid SPS avoids significant phase decomposition.
The processed alloy will have hardness above 600 HV0.5.
The processed alloy will have porosity below 1%.
The hardness increase arises from a combination of grain refinement and solute strengthening.
Conventionally cast CoCrFeNiTi has porosity and hardness of approximately 200 HV0.5.
Ti content must remain below 15 at.% to avoid HCP dominance.
A cooling rate above 10 °C/min prevents HCP formation.
The proposed falsification test uses nanoindentation at 10 mN with a 10 s dwell and TEM verification of grain refinement.
Failure of hardness to increase with verified grain refinement would falsify the claim that hardness is caused by solute strengthening rather than grain refinement.

contradictions.description: The falsification logic is reversed or ambiguous: failure of hardness to track grain refinement would undermine a grain-refinement explanation and be consistent with solute strengthening, rather than falsifying solute strengthening.

The mechanism asserts that SPS achieves full density, while the outcome permits porosity below 1% and the uncertainty explicitly allows residual porosity. These statements use inconsistent certainty about complete densification.
